notes: P04 POPETS-X03_cache_control deliverable: evaluation/venue2027/popets/cache_control.py (CACHE_CONTROL_VERSION 1.0.0) is a purpose-bound cache control layer: typed CacheKey(subject, grant, purpose, consent_epoch) 4-tuple (purpose and epoch are first-class key components, so purpose isolation is structural, not advisory), CacheEntry lines (context bytes never serialized into audit views - byte counts only), put/get with explicit PURPOSE_MISMATCH refusal on cross-purpose reads, recompute_or_fetch invoking the injected recompute callable ONLY after all refusal checks pass (never for a revoked subject, stale epoch, or mismatched purpose - refused requests produce no bytes and trigger no recomputation), and revoke(subject) invalidating EVERY entry for the subject across ALL grants, purposes and epochs, tombstoning the subject (terminal: post-revocation reads refuse REVOKED_SUBJECT and writes raise fail-closed at ANY epoch) while rotating the consent epoch exactly once per event (idempotent repeat). GUARANTEE: a revoked subject's context is never served across ANY purpose - proven executably by assert_revocation_complete(cache, subject), which scans the live entry store and raises RevocationLeakError (reason REVOCATION_LEAK, ValueError subclass) naming every surviving key. Stable uppercase reason codes throughout: HIT, RECOMPUTED, CACHE_MISS, PURPOSE_MISMATCH, EPOCH_STALE, REVOKED_SUBJECT, KEY_MALFORMED on the read path (returns, never raises); KEY_EPOCH_STALE, CONTEXT_MALFORMED, ARTIFACTS_MALFORMED, CREATED_AT_MALFORMED, SUBJECT_MALFORMED, RECOMPUTE_MALFORMED on the write path (raises CacheControlError so a lost write is never silently dropped); no hidden clock, no randomness, no network, no I/O; synthetic identifiers only. lineage_graph.py does not exist on this base, so no import of it was attempted (per task instruction a minimal self-contained layer was implemented instead). test_cache_control.py: 17 tests pass - positive: put/get round-trip per exact key with JSON-serializable byte-count views, disjoint key spaces for the same context under two purposes (separate entries, no shared hits), explicit requesting_purpose cross-read refused, recompute_or_fetch HIT on repeat and one RECOMPUTED per purpose first-use, revoke clears all purposes (3/3) with exactly-once epoch rotation and idempotent repeat, other subjects unaffected; adversarial: stale-epoch keys (both purposes) refused EPOCH_STALE with empty context, forged current-epoch key for revoked subject refused REVOKED_SUBJECT, put for revoked subject raises REVOKED_SUBJECT at any epoch, stale-epoch put raises KEY_EPOCH_STALE, assert_revocation_complete CATCHES A FORGOTTEN KEY (manually re-installed live entry for the revoked subject raises RevocationLeakError naming the key, and that entry is provably unservable through the public read path), 8 malformed input refusals with stable codes, read refusals never raise and never serve bytes, refused requests never trigger recomputation (injected callable not invoked), versioned snapshot determinism.
